searches.purpose: Locate independent field history, Moreno's foundational bibliographic record, classical process and participant requirements, methodological critique, recent intervention syntheses, Chinese randomized evidence, Portuguese-language review, ethics and current institutions while excluding drama therapy, sociodrama, ordinary role-play, simulation training and role-playing techniques embedded in another psychotherapy unless psychodrama itself is the intervention under review

items.title: Surveying 80 Years of Psychodrama Research: A Scientometric Review
items.rights_note: Open scientometric review maps publication history, influential works and research clusters across eight decades; citation prominence describes field development and does not establish therapeutic validity or a single linear origin.

items.title: Psychodrama
items.rights_note: Open Library record for a third-edition multivolume Moreno set covering psychodrama, foundations and action therapy; the copyrighted body is not cached or treated as read, and the 1964 edition must not be backdated wholesale to the earliest development of the method.

items.title: What Is Psychodrama: An Introduction to Psychodrama
items.rights_note: FEPTO-hosted introduction describes present-tense enactment, protagonist, director, auxiliaries, stage and participation capacities including reality contact and impulse control; it is a participant method account, not comparative evidence or a universal eligibility rule.

items.title: Integrative Systematic Review of Psychodrama Psychotherapy Research: Trends and Methodological Implications
items.rights_note: Open PLOS review found 31 intervention publications from 2007–2017 across heterogeneous methods and outcomes, emphasizing scarce intervention research and reporting, bias and mechanism limitations; promising results are not a pooled universal effect.

items.title: Psychodrama: Implementation, Study Design and Effectiveness: A Systematic Review
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC-ND review of 27 studies published from 2018–2022 maps implementation and outcomes but reports continuing scarcity of randomized and quasi-experimental designs; varied populations, models and techniques prevent treating psychodrama as one standardized protocol.

items.title: Effectiveness of Psychodrama on Mental Health Outcomes Based on Chinese Samples: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Studies
items.rights_note: CC BY synthesis of randomized studies in Chinese samples separates symptom alleviation from well-being promotion and notes too few eligible studies for several moderator and sensitivity analyses; estimates cannot be generalized outside the included Chinese contexts or to non-psychodrama drama interventions.

items.title: Code of Ethics and Practice for Psychodramatists
items.rights_note: FEPTO code addresses competence, contracts, confidentiality, boundaries, supervision, insurance and complaints for psychodramatists; it is professional guidance rather than adverse-event surveillance and does not replace national regulation or the ethics of a practitioner's licensed profession.

items.title: Intervenções em Psicodrama: Uma Revisão Sistemática
items.rights_note: Open Portuguese article with Portuguese, English and Spanish abstracts reviews 34 interventions across varied populations and sometimes combined theories; positive narrative conclusions and resource limitations do not supply a homogeneous effect estimate or isolate psychodrama components.

items.title: About the American Society of Group Psychotherapy and Psychodrama
items.rights_note: Official ASGPP page documents contemporary education, dissemination and professional-standards functions for psychodrama, sociometry and group psychotherapy; institutional continuation does not make those three fields synonymous or validate particular interventions.
